Subject: Draft MAP: Data handling milestones & security owners (MedSys)

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan focused on the Data Handling & Compliance milestone we discussed. I summarized the key points from our call and proposed owners/timelines so we have a single source of truth to review with your legal/security teams.

High-level recap (Data Handling & Compliance milestone)
- Objective: Ensure MedSys can meet PHI/PII constraints while using Redwood for inference with auditable retention and logging.
- Target close date: 2026-03-31 (proposal; see dependencies below).

Proposed Milestones + Owners
1) Retention policy decision (30/90/365 days) — Owner: MedSys (Legal + Security) — Due: 2026-02-22
2) Logging & audit trail spec (fields, retention, access controls) — Owner: Redwood (Priyom) + MedSys Security — Due: 2026-02-26
3) Architecture validation (hosted vs dedicated vs private) & KMS design — Owner: Redwood Infra — Due: 2026-03-05
4) Legal review & BAA/contract redlines — Owner: MedSys Legal + Redwood Legal — Due: 2026-03-15
5) Final infra test & purge verification — Owner: Redwood + MedSys IT — Due: 2026-03-25

Key constraints we noted from the call
- PHI may not be stored in persistent logs; MedSys requires the ability to purge or ensure non-persistence for flagged data.
- Complete audit trail is required for access events, configuration changes, and model output access (timestamped, user id, reason).
- All data at rest must be encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated/Private; hosted options should support CMEK or equivalent.

Dependencies / Open items
- MedSys to confirm what qualifies as PHI in scope (examples requested).
- Security questionnaire (we’ll push updated answers once we finalize logging schema).
- Legal to confirm BAA scope and any additional contractual clauses.

Attachments: MAP_Draft_v0.2.pdf (draft MAP with milestone table)

Next steps (my ask)
1) Please loop in your legal and IT/security contacts (names/emails) so we can put owners on the MAP.
2) Can you confirm a preferred retention horizon (30/90/365) for message/content logs? If unsure, we can leave as TBD and proceed with the logging schema.
3) We’ll schedule a technical session with your security team — suggested slots attached in the Drive link.

If any of the owners above should change, let me know and I’ll update the MAP. Thanks — Priyom and I will own the technical pieces and Markus will look after escalation and contract items.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the structured MAP. Quick answers and clarifications from our side: 

- PHI scope: will include any patient identifiers and clinician notes we forward to the model. Ill confirm a granular list early next week.
- Retention: top priority is the ability to prevent storage of PHI in persistent logs. For non-PHI telemetry we can accept short-term retention (30 days) but need purge capability.
- Logs: who has access to the raw logs in your hosted environment? We need assurance that Redwood personnel cannot access customer content without an approved request (audit trail).
- BAA: we need a BAA in place before any production traffic with PHI; does Redwood provide this?

Please add our legal lead (Daniel Park) and security alias (security@medsys.com) to the MAP owners. Also, can you confirm whether your hosted API supports a no-persist mode or field-level redaction prior to model invocation?

Wed like a short technical session focused only on data flows and logging — security team will attend. Preferred times next week (Feb 23-25).

Thanks,
Alicia
Director, Product Integrations | MedSys Health

Hi Alicia / Daniel —

Thanks for the clear notes. Short technical summary and options so your security/legal teams can evaluate: 

1) No-persist mode (hosted)
- We offer a configuration that disables persistent storage of request/response payloads in our long-term telemetry store (session-level ephemeral buffers only). Logs will still capture metadata (timestamps, request id, model variant) but not full content unless explicitly enabled.
- We can implement a flag at the account level to ensure no content persists and to purge existing ephemeral caches on demand.

2) Field-level redaction & client-side pre-processing
- We recommend pre-processing in MedSyss integration to remove or tokenise PHI before sending to the API. Redwood provides reference libraries and a redaction rubric (see attached logging_schema.csv stub).

3) Dedicated/Private deployment
- For full control (CMEK, VPC, on-prem), Dedicated or Private deployments provide customer-managed key options and isolated compute where logs can be routed to your S3 or SIEM.

4) Logging & audit trails
- Audit logs include access events (user, role, timestamp), config changes, and request metadata. We can export structured audit logs to your S3 bucket with a retention lifecycle you control.
- Redwood staff access requires an approved, logged request; we record any data access event and include it in the audit trail.

5) BAA & compliance artifacts
- Redwood can provide SOC 2 Type II report and standard HIPAA BAA language; legal will need to confirm specific clauses. We cannot sign a BAA until contract terms are agreed but happy to start redline.

Proposed minor adjustment to MAP timeline to allow legal review: move target close to 2026-04-08 (adds three weeks for contract & legal review). If your team prefers a tighter window, we can compress technical deliverables earlier.

Ive attached a lightweight logging schema and will prepare a brief technical deck for the security session. Suggested agenda for the session: 1) Data flow diagram 2) Retention & purge controls 3) Audit log schema + export options 4) BAA/contract next steps.

Available slots for the security deep dive: Feb 23 (10-11am PT), Feb 24 (2-3pm PT), Feb 25 (9-10am PT). Let me know which works and Ill send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
